row.evidence: Telnyx documents SAML SSO for Mission Control Portal organizations with Okta, Azure AD, Google, OneLogin, Auth0 and LastPass, and its API reference covers only listing, reading and removing organization users; no SCIM endpoint is documented.
row.notes: New row. Telnyx is a usage-priced CPaaS with no per-seat plans: Pay-as-you-go ($0 minimum), Committed ($500/mo minimum) and Enterprise ($5,000/mo minimum), so per-user fields stay null. Portal users join an organization by email invitation from the owner and get permissions through permission groups. SAML SSO (announced for 'Business accounts' in 2021) is set up with generic SAML apps in each IdP; no plan gate for SSO is stated, so sso_plan is null. The v2 REST API (bearer API key) can list, read and remove organization users and list audit logs, but cannot create or invite users, so no IdP uses it for provisioning.

scim.notes: No SCIM endpoint is documented in the help centre, the developer sitemap or the OpenAPI spec; SAML SSO is the only IdP-driven provisioning. 'false' is by absence (rule 5).

capabilities.notes: No create, invite, update or group-permission endpoints in the published OpenAPI spec; the users_groups_report endpoint reports group membership.

rate_limits.text: API: 100/sec on pay-as-you-go (standard limits); higher on Committed and Enterprise.

user_api.notes: The API is available on every account (pay-as-you-go includes 'All products available'); organization-user endpoints only list, read and remove sub-users. Invitations are sent from the portal.

okta.notes: No OIN listing (okta.com/integrations/telnyx/ is 404); vendor guide uses Okta's generic 'SAML Service Provider' app.

entra.notes: Not in Microsoft Learn's SaaS tutorial index; vendor guide uses the Entra SAML toolkit app.

google.notes: Custom SAML app per vendor guide.

onelogin.notes: SAML Test Connector (Advanced) per vendor guide.

fallbacks.notes: The 2021 release note says SAML providers 'provision Telnyx accounts for their organization members'; the help centre does not describe JIT creation or deprovisioning in detail.

open_questions: Which account types or plans can enable SSO is not stated beyond 'Business accounts' (2021 release note).
Whether SAML sign-in creates sub-users just in time, or only links invited users, is not documented in the help centre.
Whether removing an organization user via API frees anything billable or ends sessions is not documented (Telnyx has no per-seat pricing).
